title: Small sidewalks, big paperwork
question: How much paperwork does a small business carry for a few tables, a sign or a food truck?
finding: Since 2015 Public Works issued 7,501 separate sidewalk table-and-chair permits for 2,700 addresses, an average of 2.7 permits per address and as many as 16 for one. A business sign needs a building permit, which took a median 15 days and passed 4 review stations. 205 of 693 venues with an entertainment permit hold three or more different kinds of City approval at the same address. 140 of the 500 food-truck locations on the current list are still only 'requested'.
how: Public Works street-use permits by kind and address (each renewal is a new permit number); the current food-truck list; building permits for signs; Fire Department operating permits by kind; and, for addresses with an active entertainment permit, the number of different kinds of City approval on record at the same address.
limits: Yearly renewal is how the City checks insurance and conditions, and a business that changes hands starts again; both raise the count. Addresses are matched by street number and name and will mis-join some neighbours and miss others. Health permits, liquor licences (State), business registration and police permits are not in these files, so the true count is higher. The 2023 Civil Grand Jury found the City's small-business systems 'not adequately integrated' and that businesses in the fee-waiver programme 'have been charged fees that should have been waived'.
